vulnerabilities.description: GNU ncurses up to 6.5-20250322 has a stack-based buffer overflow in postprocess_termcap (tinfo/parse_entry.c) due to improper bounds checking during termcap entry processing, allowing a local attacker to trigger the overflow via a crafted termcap file, leading to denial of service.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required under normal deployment. This requires a local attacker supplying a crafted termcap entry to an interactive terminal session, which the stock container's non-interactive entrypoint does not accept.

ratings.justification: Exploitation requires a local attacker supplying a crafted termcap entry to an interactive terminal session; the stock container runs the CLI non-interactively via its entrypoint.

analysis.detail: A stack-based buffer overflow in ncurses' termcap entry parsing requires a local attacker able to supply a crafted termcap file or TERM/TERMINFO value processed by an interactive terminal session. The Liquibase Secure container runs the CLI non-interactively via its entrypoint, without accepting untrusted local termcap input; TERM is set by the container orchestration layer, not by an untrusted local actor. This OS package's version is not pinned by this repository — it tracks whatever the unversioned eclipse-temurin:21-jre-noble base image tag resolves to at build time. Confirmed by pulling the current base image directly and checking installed package versions (not from repo-pinned config), it ships libncursesw6 6.4+20240113-1ubuntu2.2, the fixed release, as additional defense-in-depth.
